Water, sewer, organics, recycling, and landfill services are included because grocery operations plausibly control produce, prep, cleaning, and packaging waste streams.

utilityDataModelingNotes: Modeled as a 4.28-million-square-foot aerospace assembly and manufacturing complex with very large but not continuous data-center-style electric load.
Electric use reflects assembly lines, compressed air, lighting, testing, offices, warehouse equipment, and a large conditioned volume; summer months are higher due to ventilation and cooling loads.
Gas is modeled for space heating, large-volume ventilation makeup air, process support, and finishing-area heating with clear winter seasonality.

Water and sewer include industrial support, cooling/process makeup, restrooms, cafeteria/service areas, and limited landscape needs, with an irrigation meter represented for campus-scale outdoor uses.
Waste includes industrial landfill, recycling, metals/materials recovery, and lower organics compared with food manufacturing.
No source URLs were checked; values rely only on the supplied sample profile fields.

utilityDataModelingNotes: Square footage is unknown in the supplied profile, so this fixture assumes roughly six million square feet of active fab, cleanroom, utility, office, and support space within the larger 700-acre campus context.
Electric load is modeled as continuous high-load-factor semiconductor fabrication with cleanrooms, process tools, pumps, chilled water, exhaust, and redundancy loads.
Gas is included because Southwest Gas is supplied and process/boiler support is plausible, but gas is smaller than electric for this semiconductor fixture.
Water use is intentionally very high to exercise industrial water-intensity, reclaimed-water, and process-cooling logic; values are synthetic and not actual campus withdrawals.
Waste is modeled as industrial/commercial fixture data only and does not attempt to represent regulated hazardous-waste manifests.
No source URLs were checked; values rely only on the supplied sample profile fields.

utilityDataModelingNotes: Modeled as a 17-million-square-foot public university campus with laboratories, residence halls, dining, athletics, libraries, healthcare-adjacent spaces, offices, and campus operations.
Electric use includes research equipment, ventilation, chilled-water and district-energy auxiliaries, IT, lighting, dining, residence halls, and athletic/event spaces.
Gas is modeled as campus-scale institutional service with district-energy and heating-plant complexity; values are synthetic and not tariff- or plant-meter-accurate.
Water and sewer include student housing, labs, dining, athletics, cooling support, landscape irrigation, and campus custodial loads.
Waste includes campus landfill, recycling, organics, move-out, event, dining, and laboratory-adjacent nonhazardous streams; hazardous and regulated waste are intentionally not itemized.
No source URLs were checked; values rely only on the supplied sample profile fields.

utilityDataModelingNotes: Modeled as a 469,000-square-foot tribal healthcare campus with hospital, outpatient care, pharmacy, laboratory, clinical administration, emergency, and community-health functions.
Electric use reflects healthcare ventilation, clinical loads, imaging, pharmacy and lab equipment, kitchen/service loads, and critical 24/7 operations.
Gas is high for healthcare because domestic hot water, heating, humidification, kitchen, laundry-like service, and clinical comfort requirements are represented.
Water and sewer reflect clinical functions, domestic hot water, sterilization/support, food service, restrooms, and campus irrigation.
Waste includes generic landfill, recycling, food-service, and overage costs; regulated medical waste is not itemized because it is outside the allowed generic waste fields.
No source URLs were checked; values rely only on the supplied sample profile fields.
